analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (20.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 202bps to 7176 (+5% YTD), its sixth straight daily decline and longest streak since 2024, after a roughly 400bps intraday reversal with no major headline.
Drivers cited for the selloff: the Hunterbrook short report on AMD and fears of US strikes on Iran. Kospi fell 6%, with Samsung and SK Hynix each down 7%.
Levels at the time of writing: US 10-year yield 5.01%, Brent $92, gold $3,547, Bitcoin $62k.
Next week's focus: PCE inflation (Wednesday) and earnings from Dell, Best Buy and others.
Middle East: Trump is weighing another round of extensive military strikes on Iran, based on new intelligence on Iranian capabilities and pressure from Israel to act quickly and aggressively.

Hunterbrook's AMD short report argues investors underestimate AMD's China export-restriction exposure. AMD billed 22.4% of FY2025 revenue to China and Hong Kong customers versus 9.1% for Nvidia. Tighter licensing could slow AI accelerator sales.
The report says Chinese server maker IEIT incorporated at least six newer versions of AMD firmware after the US blacklisted it.

GS analysis of 453 large-cap mutual funds ($3.9tr equity assets): funds continued to see outflows, were underweight AI-exposed equities ahead of recent poor performance, and were 722bp underweight the Mag 7 at end of Q3 2026.
GS finds funds deliver their best excess returns when return dispersion is wide and market breadth is not narrow.

GS recommends shorting European Staples (GSXESTAP) on rich valuation, unexciting earnings and low dividend yield versus fixed income, after the sector's best monthly performance on record in October. The report says US colleagues are also shorting the sector.

GS asset allocation: modestly pro-risk. Slowing earnings growth and potentially higher volatility imply lower risk-adjusted returns. It favours selective growth alongside quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks, and says bonds should offer a better buffer against equity weakness.
CTA positioning in US equities is short almost $10bn, the lowest since April. For the first time in weeks, flows from the cohort are skewed asymmetrically to the upside.

GS 2027 US equity forecast: S&P 500 up 17% to 8700, against a 21% annualized return over the past four years. EPS growth slows from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. P/E fell 19% in 2026, sits near its 10-year average and is expected to stay near 18x.

GS prefers equities to credit because tight spreads, releveraging and rising issuance limit credit returns. It cites the late-1990s, when equities kept rising with more volatility while credit lagged.
Gold: GS sees near-term downside risk and elevated volatility as the Fed continues to hike, but still forecasts $4,650 by end-2027 on central bank purchases.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week versus an average weekly inflow of $6.2bn over the prior four weeks. They lost $5.6bn on Monday alone and saw outflows on each of the last three days.

Other items: Apple is building an AI agent that operates apps, websites and code for users. GTA 6 pre-orders and first-day sales exceeded 24.5m units (about $2.36bn). SpaceX designed a miniature rooftop cell tower to remove dead zones.

market_movers.rationale: The note relays Hunterbrook's short report on AMD's China export-restriction exposure (22.4% of FY2025 revenue billed to China and Hong Kong) and lists it among the day's selloff drivers. GS does not state its own view.
Nvidia faces the same China export restrictions, with 9.1% of revenue billed to China and Hong Kong versus 22.4% for AMD. A GS semis podcast covered NVDA earnings, financing and power constraints.
The WMT CEO said on the earnings call that Holiday Meal basket prices on unchanged items are down about 12% and that it has sold 1 million more turkeys than a year ago.

sector_views.rationale: GS likes shorting European Staples on rich valuation, unexciting earnings and low dividend yield versus fixed income, after record monthly performance in October.
The note says US colleagues are also shorting the sector.
Semis ETFs saw $7.3bn of outflows last week. The note adds no GS view on the sector.

earnings_insights: Next week's earnings focus: Dell, Best Buy and others. The note gives no estimates.
WMT reported earnings; the CEO's call remarks on the Holiday Meal basket are quoted. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.
GS 2027 forecast: S&P 500 EPS growth slows from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The 10-year is above 5% during a six-day equity decline.
The note lists PCE as next week's main macro focus and gives no estimate.
GS sees near-term downside risk but a grind higher on central bank purchases.
GS's base case is that elevated rates and AI uncertainty hold the P/E near its current 18x.
The note says the Fed is still hiking, which is the reason GS gives for near-term gold downside risk.

crypto_views: Bitcoin was at $62k on 20 Nov 2026 during the equity selloff. The note adds no further crypto view.

trade_ideas.rationale: Rich valuation, unexciting earnings and low dividend yield versus fixed income, after the sector's best monthly performance on record in October.

risk_factors: A further US strike on Iran.
Tighter China export licensing for AI accelerators, which the AMD short report says AMD is more exposed to than Nvidia.
Sustained semis ETF outflows and a longer equity losing streak.
Elevated rates, with the 10-year at 5.01% and the Fed still hiking, and AI uncertainty capping the P/E near 18x.
Slowing earnings growth and potentially higher volatility, which GS says lower risk-adjusted returns.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs are short almost $10bn of US equities, the lowest since April. Flows from the cohort are skewed asymmetrically to the upside for the first time in weeks.
Mutual funds were 722bp underweight the Mag 7 at end of Q3 2026 and underweight AI-exposed equities.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week against an average weekly inflow of $6.2bn over the prior four weeks, including $5.6bn on Monday.
GS asset allocation flags potentially higher volatility and lower risk-adjusted returns.
geopolitical: Trump is weighing another round of extensive US military strikes on Iran, citing new intelligence on Iranian capabilities and Israeli pressure to move quickly and aggressively.
The AMD short report centres on US export restrictions on China and the blacklisting of Chinese server maker IEIT.
cross_bank_references: Our US colleagues are also shorting the sector (US staples, within Goldman Sachs).

tension_points.bull_case: GS forecasts the S&P 500 up 17% to 8700 in 2027, with a solid economy and AI investment driving robust but decelerating EPS growth (30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027).
tension_points.bear_case: The same note flags slowing earnings growth, potentially higher volatility, and elevated rates plus AI uncertainty holding P/E near 18x. The S&P was down six days in a row, with the 10-year at 5.01%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further cut in the P/E from the 18x base case, or EPS growth falling below the 18% forecast for 2027.
